description: Solve a captcha in the active web page. With `provider: "auto"` (default) it dispatches: a Google reCAPTCHA widget (v2 checkbox / image grid / audio, or v3 token) is solved by the reCAPTCHA solver; otherwise it solves a rotation-dial (rotate-the-disc / radial slider) captcha by dragging it round. Dial path: repeats reading the next angle from angleScript, dragging the knob there with real pointer moves, screenshotting the widget and scoring it with judgeScript (and/or checking successScript), re-showing and refreshing, then stopping when it passes. Each press is absolute (live start angle to target in one drag), so nothing has to accumulate between presses; a fit the script rates low can buy a new picture with minAngleConfidence instead of a hopeless drag. For reCAPTCHA the image grid is classified by the configured vision endpoint (APPIUM_MCP_CAPTCHA_VLM_URL, or the claude-local hunch config) or, when none is configured, by the MCP client model through sampling, and re-solved each round. Selector- and script-driven, so it is not tied to any site. Use playwright_frames first to find the widget frame, and playwright_evaluate for one-off probes.

angleScript.description: JS run in the widget frame before each attempt; returns the next end angle in degrees, or { angle, direction } ("cw" | "ccw" | "shortest"). It may also return { startAngle, radius, grab } to override the dial geometry: startAngle and radius in the same convention as playwright_drag_arc, grab as {x, y} px from the dial box top-left. Use those when the knob is not an element, and derive the grab from live state every call (a range input value mapped along its track) — the script is re-run when a drag has to be repeated, so a stale constant grab would press the wrong place. For a linear control add `track: { x1, y1, x2, y2 }` (px from the dial box top-left) with `min`/`max` (the control's value range, default 0–360): the drag then runs straight along that line with startAngle and angle read as values, which is what a range input needs — an arc leaves the track and the value stops updating. Inset the line by half the thumb width at both ends so the extremes are reachable. Keep any search-window state in a window variable so it shrinks as attempts go on. Land the final precision in `angle`: a drag is absolute (startAngle from live state to `angle` in one press), so deltas do not have to accumulate across presses, and on widgets that re-fit or redraw themselves nothing set by an earlier press survives — a sequence of small corrections is a sequence of absolute drags, never wheel ticks that add up. Return `confidence` (0–1) when the fit is scored from evidence (spread and peak of candidate answers): the tool logs it, and with minAngleConfidence a low value asks for a new picture instead of spending a hopeless drag.

beforeNext.description: CSS selector clicked before every attempt after the first — a control the widget hides itself behind (re-show links, "try again" buttons).

capture.description: CSS selector of the region to screenshot for judgeScript. Default: the dial box. Widen it with pad when the judgement needs the surround.

dial.description: CSS selector of the dial body of a rotate-the-disc captcha (rotation dial / radial slider): the disc or its rotation track, e.g. "#dial" or ".rotation-disc". Required for the dial provider.

frame.description: Frame holding the widget, from playwright_frames. Default "main". Captcha widgets are normally cross-origin iframes and must be named here.

handle.description: CSS selector of the knob riding the disc rim, e.g. "#handle". Its current bearing gives the start angle and its box centre the press point. Omit it when the knob is not an element (a range-input thumb, a canvas sprite) and let angleScript return startAngle/radius/grab instead. Its box alone is wrong for a range thumb: that box spans the whole track. Also drop it when a cursor-hotspot knob on screen has no computable cursor — a `<input type=range>` thumb with `cursor: auto` reports nothing, so derive the grab from the control value instead.

holdMs.description: Pause between releasing the drag and taking the screenshot (default 600). Drop it once settled; raise it for a slow widget.

identityScript.description: JS run in the main frame; returns a stable string that names the current challenge (a session token in a hidden field, an image src). Read before the drag and again before judging: a picture replaced mid-attempt makes the screenshot meaningless, so the score is skipped and the attempt counts as a miss. Use a value that outlives image fetches — a per-image URL is replaced by the widget's own refresh, not by this.

judgeScript.description: JS run in the main frame after each attempt with one argument: { image, width, height, dial, handle, angle, attempt }. `image` is a data URL PNG of the capture region, so the script can draw it to a canvas and score it. Return truthy / a score / { ok, score, note }. Use it when the picture must be judged by code (a seam line, an alignment offset) rather than assumed passed.

maxAgeMs.description: Challenges that expire (a signed image URL, roughly a minute) get replaced when the current one is older than this: the refresh control is clicked and the clock resets. Default 55000. Cards that hand out a stable per-session token are safe to keep much longer (20 s is comfortable); a per-image URL is the case that needs a short value.

maxMs.description: Wall-clock cap for the whole call (default 90000).

minAngleConfidence.description: Gate on the confidence angleScript reports. Below it, the challenge is refreshed rather than dragged: an adversarial puzzle whose fit is a coin toss is a burnt attempt, and a fresh picture is cheaper. Agreement between candidate answers should drive that number, not peak — on a live widget a genuine fit peaks lower than a hopeless one can, so a peak-only floor vetoes good drags. Around 0.35 is a sensible gate. Costs one attempt per refresh, and does nothing without `refresh` (the drag proceeds; only the log records the low value).

pad.description: Padding around the capture box, px (default 32).

passScore.description: When judgeScript returns a bare number, score at or above this counts as passed (default 0.9).

provider.description: Which captcha to solve. "auto" (default) picks reCAPTCHA when its widget is on the page and the rotation dial otherwise (or whenever `dial` is given). "recaptcha" covers Google reCAPTCHA v2 (checkbox, image grid, audio) and v3 token capture; its dedicated tool playwright_captcha_recaptcha takes the same arguments directly. Cloudflare Turnstile has its own tool, playwright_captcha_turnstile.

refresh.description: CSS selector of the widget’s reload control, clicked between attempts. Without it the same challenge is retried.

settleMs.description: Wait after a drag (and after a refresh) before judging, default 900.

settleScript.description: JS run in the widget frame, polled until truthy: the widget has finished moving and has accepted the drag. Use it wherever a load animation can overwrite a value set mid-flight, or the widget records a "user moved it" flag that submit refuses without. Polled after a refresh and after every drag; a drag that never settles is repeated (twice) before the attempt is judged, and counts as a miss unless successScript passes. Keep the check on live state (control value equals the target AND the widget's own touched flag), with the target stashed by angleScript in a window variable.

settleTimeoutMs.description: How long settleScript may stay falsy before a drag counts as unrecorded (default 2500).

successScript.description: JS run in the main frame after each attempt; truthy when the captcha passed. Prefer the token field ("the hidden response field now has a value") over the picture. Optional when judgeScript is given, but keep it when one exists — it is the reliable half of the verdict. Test a value that only exists after success (a now-revealed number or token), not a wrapper's innerText: dialogs keep their static strings ("the code expired") in that text at all times, so it never distinguishes a pass.

name: playwright_captcha_solve
